title: California coast Tue Nov 24: Arena Cove observed 8.86 ft MLLW, above the 8.67 ft listed record (1998) and every later high WALTER read; Humboldt (North Spit) 10.16 ft, under January's 10.36; San Francisco 8.23 ft with 8.5 forecast Wed, 'approaching the highest tide ever recorded'
body:
# California tides, Tue Nov 24 (CO-OPS verified-pending data) and Wednesday's forecast

| Gauge | Observed high 11/24 | Highest found before | Reads as | Forecast Wed Nov 25 (NWS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Arena Cove (9416841) | **8.862 (9:24 AM PST)** | 8.67 listed (1998-02-06); later highs read: 8.65 (Jan 3 2026), 8.55 (Jan 2023), 8.43 (Dec 2024) | **above all found** | not read |
| North Spit, Humboldt (9418767) | 10.162 (10:18 AM PST) | 10.36 (Jan 3 2026) | under | 10.0 to 10.4, straddles 10.36 |
| Crescent City (9419750) | 10.062 (10:00 AM PST) | 10.66 listed (1983) | under | not read |
| San Francisco (9414290) | 8.233 (10:06 AM PST) | record not read by WALTER | not established | 8.5 ft at 10:49 AM Wed, 'approaching the highest tide ever recorded' (NWS text) |

- **Why IMMEDIATE:** an observed level above the highest found at Arena Cove (step 7j, routing v0.53). Preliminary water-level data; NOAA verifies later; other years were not all read. Card 030's Humboldt forecast (10.3 to 11.0) was NOT met: the high was 10.16.
- **Still live:** Coastal Flood Warnings for Humboldt, Del Norte, southwest Humboldt and Mendocino from 9 AM to 1 PM PST Wed ('major flooding in low lying areas mainly around Humboldt Bay'; waves up to 25 feet); San Francisco and San Pablo shorelines to Thu 4 PM PST (up to 2.7 ft inundation; High Surf Warning, 20 to 30 foot waves, midnight Tue to midnight Wed); Point Reyes to Big Sur Wed; Orange and San Diego to Fri; San Luis Obispo to Ventura to Thu noon.
- **King Salmon (Humboldt):** a local outlet reported an evacuation order effective 7:00 AM PST Tue and a proclaimed local emergency (Lost Coast Outpost 11/23, read by a helper); damage after the tide not read.
- **One card per state per check;** Florida is on 005.

Economic channel is AEOLUS's read.

title: Florida floods Tue Nov 24 evening: Sanford reached major (8.20 ft), DeLand 5.73 with 6.2 forecast by Nov 29 (record 6.33), Cocoa 18.44, Lake Harney 13.14; new coastal flood warnings from Nassau to Flagler for Wednesday; flood watches still up in southeast and east-central Florida
body:
# Florida flood status (NWS gauges 21:15 to 21:30 ET 11/24)

| Gauge | Observed | Was (11/23) | Forecast | Record |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cocoa | 18.44 ft | 18.58 | 18.5 (11/25); 18.4 to 18.5 through the weekend (NWS) | 17.55 (1953) before this event |
| Lake Harney | 13.14 ft | 13.09 | near 13.1 through midweek, then a very slow fall | 12.67 (2022) exceeded |
| Sanford | **8.20 ft (major, over 8.0)** | 7.75 (moderate) | 8.4 | 8.96 (2022) |
| DeLand | 5.73 ft | 5.51 | **6.2 by 11/29** (was 6.1) | 6.33 (2022): 0.13 under |
| Astor | 4.16 ft | 4.14 | 4.4 | 4.81 (2024) |

- **New since the last check:** Coastal Flood Warnings for coastal Duval, St. Johns, Nassau, Flagler and Putnam (with Glynn and Camden, GA): Wed 1 AM to 7 PM EST for most; Flagler until 7 PM Wed.
- **Flood watches:** southeast (Palm Beach, Broward, Miami-Dade) from 7 PM Tue through late Wed night; east-central (Brevard, Indian River, St. Lucie, Martin, Okeechobee) 1 AM Wed through late Wed night: 1 to 2 inches, locally 3 to 4.
- **Card 025's and 017's facts change only as above.** The DeLand record line (6.33 ft) is the thing to watch from Thursday.
- WESH 11/23: the governor's second, broader federal request was announced, not yet filed; the first is pending (helper read). No federal declaration read since.
